Then, at $x = 0$, $f$ is
options: differentiable and the derivative is not continuous
differentiable and the derivative is continuous
questions.solution:
Given function&

$f\left(x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}\dfrac{sin\left(x^{2}\right)}{x} & , x \ne 0 \\ 0 & , ifx = 0\end{cases}\right$

then $\lim_{x \to 0}f\left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{sinx^{2}}{x} = \lim_{x \to 0}$

$x\dfrac{sinx^{2}}{x2} = 0 = f \left(0\right)$

Hence, $f \left(x\right)$ is continuous at $x = 0$

Now, for differentiability

$RHD$ (at $x = 0$)

$= \lim_{h \to 0}\d$ dfrac{f$\left(0 + h\right) - f\left(0\right)}{h} = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{$ sinh^{2}}{h2} =1$

and $LHD$ (at $x = 0$)

$= \lim_{h \to 0}\d$ dfrac{f\left(0 - h\right) - f \left(0\right)}${- h} = \lim_{h \to $0}\dfrac{ sinh^{2}}{h2} =1$

So, $f\left(x\right)$ is differentiable at $x = 0$

$∴ f^{'}\left(x\right) = \$ left[$$\begin{cases}2cos \left(x^{2}\right) - \dfrac{sinx^{2}}{x2}& , ifx \ne 0 \\ 1 & , ifx = 0\end{cases}$$\right]$

$∵ \lim_{x \to 0}f^{'} $\left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to 0} \lleft[2cos\left(x^{2}\right) - \dfrac{sinx^{2}}{x2}\right]$

$= 2 - 1 = 1$

$∴ \lim_{x \to 0}f^{'} \left($ x\right) = f^{'} $\left(0\right)$

So, $f \left($ x\right)$ is differentiable and the derivative is continuous.

questions.q: Let $f: \left(- 1, 1\right) \to R$ be a differentiable function satisfying $\left(f^{'} \left(x\right)\right)^{4} = 16\l$ left(f$\left(x\right)\right)^{2}$ for all $x \in \left(-1, 1\right)$ f$\left(0\right) =$$0$ The number of such functions is
questions.solution:
It is given that, 

${\left({f}^{'}\left(x\right)\right)}^{4} = 16{\left(f\left(x\right)\right)}^{2}, ∀ x \in \left(- 1, 1\right)$

$⇒ {\left({f}^{'}\left(x\right)\right)}^{2} = \pm 4f\left(x\right)$

Case $I$ 

If $f\left(x\right) \ge 0 ∀ x \in \left(- 1, 1\right)$

Then, ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \pm 2\sqrt{f\left(x\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{f}^{'}\left(x\right)}{\sqrt{f\left(x\right)}} = \pm 2$

$⇒ 2\sqrt{f\left(x\right)} = \pm 2x, \left[∵ f\left(0\right) = 0\right]$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {x}^{2} ∀ x \in \left(- 1, 1\right)$

Case $II$ 

If $f\left(x\right) < 0 ∀ x \in \left(- 1, 1\right)$

Then, ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \pm 2\sqrt{- f\left(x\right)}$

$∴ f\left(x\right) = - {x}^{2} ∀ x \in \left(- 1, 1\right)$

$∴ {f}_{1}\left(x\right) = \left[\begin{array}{ll}{x}^{2}, 0 \le x < 1 \\ {x}^{2}, - 1 < x < 0\end{array}\right$

${f}_{2}\left(x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}{x}^{2} & , 0 \le x < 1 \\ - {x}^{2} & - 1 < x < 0\end{cases}\right$

${f}_{3}\left(x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}- {x}^{2} & , 0 \le x < 1 \\ {x}^{2} & , - 1 < x < 0\end{cases}\right$

${f}_{4}\left(x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}- {x}^{2} & , 0 \le x < 1 \\ - {x}^{2} & , - 1 < x < 0\end{cases}\right$

${f}_{5}\left(x\right) = 0$

${f}_{6}\left(x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}0 & , 0 \le x < 1 \\ {x}^{2} & , - 1 < x < 0\end{cases}, \ldots\right$ and so on.

Hence, there are more than $4$ functions possible.
